newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish budget gap at 63 pct of '96 plan in Jan-Oct.
newsitem.headline: Polish budget gap at 63 pct of '96 plan in Jan-Oct.

text.p: The Polish budget deficit after 10 months of this year accounted for 63.1 percent of the planned 10.16 billion zloty shortfall for the whole of 1996, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Tuesday.
Kolodko told a Senate committee debating 1997 taxes, that revenues collected over the period accounted for 79.7 percent of the 1996 plan and spending accounted for 78.2 percent.
Kolodko gave no further figures. The finance ministry is due to release official budget data for the January-October period on November 15. @

In September the budget shortfall amounted to 6.15 billion zlotys, or 60.5 percent of the 1996 plan, with revenues at 70.02 billion and expenditures at 76.17 billion. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
